forecaster_note: Winds have gone offshore and it's clean, fun-sized surf this morning — chest to around head high at the south exposures, smaller but rideable elsewhere. NE seabreeze crumbles most spots in the arvo (S-facing stays cleaner), and a long-period S swell may start filling in late. — Surfline forecaster (Hugh's Monday NSW update)

wind.summary: Light NNW 7 kph — offshore/cross-shore now. Swings NE onshore ~17–19 kph from noon, gusts to ~33 by evening.

shark.summary: No shark detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly — or anywhere Palm Beach to Manly — in the last 24h. Feed is current (newest statewide detection ~1.5h old; 39 real detections statewide in 24h, none on the Northern Beaches).

days.label: Today
days.note: Fun, clean morning: light offshore, S swell 4.3ft/9s (281 kJ) plus a NE 3.3ft/10s. Long Reef is the pick — it's S-facing and uses the S swell, while Dee Why gets the dead-S angle wrapping badly. Get in before ~10am; NE seabreeze from noon. High tide 9:31am.

dee-why.window: Go now until ~9:30am: light NW off the land, then it swings NE onshore by noon. The NE 64° swell is the good stuff here; the dead-S 176° energy wraps badly, so skip the rights on that.

tip.label: Read the NE, ignore the S
tip.text: Dominant energy is dead-S (~176°) — the angle that doesn't work at the Point. Frontside rights are a trap on that; the NE 3.3ft/10s is the clean part. Take the peaks that line up off the NE, and use the backside lefts when the S is doing the work.

long-reef.window: Best of the four this morning: S-facing, so it actually uses the 4.3ft S swell, with light offshore till ~9am. Arvo NE seabreeze crumbles it, though S-facing stays cleaner than most.

tip.label: Best bank wins
tip.text: Reef takes the S swell well. Frontside rights off the reef — pick the peak with shape rather than paddling for the biggest set.

curl-curl.window: Solid chest-to-head peaks with a light offshore early. Fades to a NE bump after noon.

tip.label: Good early alternative
tip.text: Take the beachie peaks in the first couple of hours — S swell gets in here better than at Dee Why.

manly.window: Smaller and more sheltered from the S — clean-ish early but gets bumpy with the NE after noon.

tip.label: Sheltered fallback
tip.text: Least S energy of the four — softer, but the tidiest when the seabreeze arrives.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The regular Wednesday long-period S swell shows up: head to overhead at the S exposures with a wait between sets and real power. Offshore morning, NE arvo. Long Reef/Curl Curl over Dee Why. Sizes estimated from the forecaster text.

dee-why.window: Offshore morning then NE arvo. Long-period S wraps poorly at the Point — expect it smaller and inconsistent here vs the S exposures.
